session_states.stopping: interrupt and process clean-up in progress
session_states.stopped: turn interrupted, processes confirmed gone; needs settle
session_states.leftover: processes not confirmed gone; locks held
session_states.paused_unanswered: the unanswered-request policy fired; needs settle
session_states.paused_for_update: a new Codex binary appeared while the turn only waited for an answer; needs settle
session_states.completed_needs_review: turn completed, processes confirmed gone; needs settle
session_states.uncertain: the runtime died mid-turn; needs settle

request_kinds.command: {command, cwd, reason, network: {host, protocol} | null, escalation, gate_hint}
request_kinds.fileChange: {files: [{path, change: add | delete | update | rename, moved_to?, added, removed}], reason, grant_root?, outside_workspace: [...]}
request_kinds.question: {questions: [{id, header, question, options, allow_other}]}
request_kinds.site: {host, protocol: http | https | null}: a site Codex's network proxy blocked a command from reaching, asked of the owner; not one of Codex's requests
request_kinds.paths: relative to the root; outside paths are absolute and listed

allowed_decisions_rules: computed by RAVIS, so no client can grant more than it offers
Codex's acceptForSession and a permissions grant with scope session are never offered in this delivery
writes outside the root, or a denied path, offer only skip and stop
a secret question is never offered: RAVIS answers it empty itself and emits request.resolved {by: policy_secret}
a question offers answer and stop (derived from Clarvis's rendering: each option, typing when allow_other, Stop the run)

a request asking for network access (a command's networkApprovalContext or additionalPermissions.network, or a permission grant's network) offers only skip and stop: approvals never open the network on Codex 0.154.0, and internet access comes from the owner's approved-sites allowlist

a site request offers allow_site and keep_blocked: one is open at a time, each host is asked once per task, it never pauses the task, and it stays open after the turn ends until the owner decides or the task ends; allow_site adds exactly that host to Codex's allowlist while it runs (never a wildcard, an IP address or a local name) and emits site.allowed

unanswered_request_policy.attached: a window counts as attached while its Clarvis panel's presence is under 45 s old; the request waits, and after 2 hours the policy fires
unanswered_request_policy.detached: the menu bar and dashboard show the wait at once; after 30 minutes the policy fires
unanswered_request_policy.when_it_fires: RAVIS answers with the stop response, runs the end sequence, the session becomes paused_unanswered, the thread is kept, and request.resolved {by: policy_timeout} is emitted
unanswered_request_policy.never: RAVIS never answers accept, acceptForSession or a grant on the owner's behalf, and never auto-approves while no window is attached

rules: the body carries no sandbox, permission-profile or approval-policy fields: RAVIS derives them from mode, the owner's file-rules decision and the calibration record, so a client can't weaken them
limits.max_steps comes from clarvis.agent.maxStepsPerTask, and RAVIS enforces it even while no window is attached
creation takes the project lock and the checkout lock file atomically, or takes the lock over from lock.transfer_token
Clarvis's key is sha256(taskId + ":" + windowId + ":" + attempt)
